rationale: A is stronger overall because it provides a more complete evidence chain from compatibility through blind comparison and a real-workflow trial, and its cache key, full-weight hashing, champion snapshot, uniform rerun rule after threshold changes, and explicit separation of evaluation from adoption make the process more reproducible and resistant to favouritism. B is somewhat more aggressively fail-fast, but its partial-weight fingerprint can falsely treat materially different releases as identical, its single manually scored probe can reject a candidate on noise, and its watch/adopt rules conflict with its claim that every failed stage is an immediate rejection. A still has weaknesses—notably an underpowered one-standard-error comparison rule, potentially unrealistic timing, and model identity that should also cover configuration and tokenizer artefacts—but its reasoning is deeper and its promotion evidence is more credible.
